scope: Exactly the twenty ordered staged Sentry originals in the supplied index. All 2954 numbered original lines were read completely in untruncated chunks of at most 100 staging lines; staging has 3014 lines including wrappers. This is prerequisite research, not a scan, code/security audit, skill execution, vulnerability finding or approval. No source instructions, examples, helpers, tests, scans, model/network requests, package setup, permission changes or live-account operations were executed. new_executions counts researched-workflow executions, not inert local file-reading and report-writing utilities. The prospective default frozen runtime is isolated, non-root, offline standard-library Python. Reviewed-offline expansion is approved in principle, not already reviewed or installed. Every expansion needs concrete unchanged public input, provenance and licenses, exact dependency/tool closure, task-specific command and filesystem controls, no outside access, and independent verifiers before freeze. Missing prerequisites narrow task fidelity; they are not final source exclusions. No hosted account, service or accelerator requirement is inferred merely from a framework name.
linked_reference_caveat: Only the supplied originals and index were read. Linked pages, bundled references, scripts, assets, external implementation code and live state were not fetched or read; descriptions of their behavior are source-stated, not independently verified. Existing staged address placeholders were retained; a residual hostname was masked in the reading output to avoid transmitting it further. Original blob identifiers and SHA-256 values are copied exactly in index order; hashes were not recomputed from normalized staging and do not authenticate unavailable raw blobs. Citations use original per-source line ranges with digits-only citation bounds, never staging positions. Workflow and prerequisites are grounded in the citations; offline feasibility and verifier recommendations are analytical conclusions. Examples are not actual task datasets. Drafts and stubs are not genuine commits, hosted operations, publication, native renders or security guarantees. Measured behavior is distinct from human quality judgment, and original empirical claims remain unverified.

sources.workflow: Inspect repository manifests, lockfiles, commands, policies and code conventions; choose root or narrower scope; write concise reference-backed agent instructions and, only if required, a compatible symlink.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The original requires a target repository, its existing documentation and command definitions, knowledge of subtree differences, and verification of named paths and commands. It targets fewer than 60 lines with an absolute 100-line maximum. Package-manager examples are illustrative, not universal dependencies. A Claude-compatible entrypoint and symlink support are conditional.
sources.offline_assessment: An unchanged licensed public repository snapshot is the actual missing task input. Python can inspect files, count lines and draft deterministic edits offline; command-existence checks do not authorize execution. Real symlink behavior needs a reviewed writable sandbox and platform semantics. No hosted account, model endpoint or accelerator is intrinsically needed.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Check every cited path against the frozen repository, command definitions against configuration, line limits, scope precedence and absence of divergent instruction copies. A maintainer must judge which conventions are useful and non-obvious; path and length checks cannot establish instruction quality or prove commands safe.

sources.workflow: Write user-facing copy in Plain Speech by default, using expressive Sentry Voice only for appropriate contexts while preserving functional meaning.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The original supplies tone-selection, grammar, punctuation and component-specific rules. Actual inputs are the requested UI/document context, intended message, action and consequences. The two linked brand and frontend references are unread pointers, not supplied complete rubrics. No executable toolchain or hosted account is stated.
sources.offline_assessment: Offline drafting and rule-based checks fit Python once concrete unchanged public input and its license are reviewed. The original itself provides enough rules for a bounded copy exercise, but full compliance with unread handbooks cannot be claimed. Drafting a transactional message or documentation does not send or publish it.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Check measurable restrictions such as button length, capitalization and punctuation against a fixture-specific rubric. Human review must assess tone selection, empathy, clarity, accurate consequences and whether personality obscures meaning. Brand-reference completeness requires separate reference review; subjective quality has no complete deterministic oracle.

sources.workflow: Infer repository stack and integrations, examine existing settings, and recommend read-only command permissions, optional connectors and merge instructions without applying them.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The original asks for repository structure, manifests/lockfiles, existing Claude settings and connector configuration. It lists shell, Git, service and stack-specific commands but says to include only detected tools and exclude state-changing commands. Sentry/Linear connectors, credentials and service slugs are conditional recommendations, not necessary inputs for local recommendation drafting.
sources.offline_assessment: A frozen licensed public repository and inert configuration fixture permit Python inventory and JSON drafting. Listed commands must not be executed or auto-approved. Broad argument wildcards and read-only labels do not establish safety; package queries and service commands can have network or other effects. Exact arguments, configuration schema, dependencies and controls require review before expansion. No live permissions or connector activation is in scope.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Validate JSON and merge preservation, tie recommendations to observed lockfiles, and check package-manager exclusivity. A separate command-policy review must evaluate argument restrictions, subprocesses, network effects and connector permissions. The original read-only objective is a requirement, not a verified guarantee of its sample allowlist.

sources.workflow: Review a specified change for runtime, performance, compatibility, security, architecture and test-coverage concerns; provide actionable feedback and escalate higher-impact decisions.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The original assumes concrete code changes, surrounding architecture, requirements and tests. Django/React snippets illustrate patterns rather than mandate frameworks. Schema, API, dependency, performance-critical and security-sensitive changes call for senior engineering attention. Linked engineering guidelines are unread external context.
sources.offline_assessment: A licensed public base/head snapshot with tests and requirements supports bounded local analysis in Python; no PR account is necessary merely to draft feedback. Framework test execution needs reviewed dependencies and sandboxed commands. No code review or security audit was performed here, and a text review would not constitute hosted approval.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Independent regression or behavioral checks support concrete bug and performance claims under reviewed conditions. Architecture fit, test adequacy, risk tolerance and approval are human judgments. Verify context and uncertainty rather than equating pattern matches or a clean report with a security guarantee.

sources.workflow: Simplify recently modified code for clarity and consistency while retaining existing behavior, applying project-specific standards and avoiding indiscriminate scope expansion.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The original requires actual changed code and project standards from its instruction file. ES-module, React and TypeScript examples do not impose a service or fixed language on every input. Exact functional preservation and a recent-change boundary are explicit. The upstream attribution link is not a loaded implementation or behavioral specification.
sources.offline_assessment: Deterministic editing is viable in offline Python on a concrete frozen public repository. Existing tests, fixtures, language runtimes and dependencies are additional inputs for stronger validation; TypeScript/React tooling needs reviewed expansion. A rewrite alone establishes neither equivalent behavior nor improved maintainability. No hosted account is inherent.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Compare behavior before/after with independent covering tests, including side effects and edge cases, in a reviewed toolchain. Check nominated scope and project conventions. Clarity, useful abstractions and maintainability require human assessment; passing a few tests cannot prove universal equivalence.

sources.workflow: Draft a conventional commit message or create one coherent local commit, checking branch safety and using suitable issue and breaking-change footers.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The original covers both drafting and committing, requires branch inspection and usually a feature branch when starting on a primary branch, and specifies allowed types/message limits. Actual creation needs a target Git repository, intended changes, index state and local author/committer identity. Verified issue identifiers are conditional; sample identifiers are not task data. No push or hosted service is required.
sources.offline_assessment: Python can draft and check messages from supplied change facts. An authentic offline commit is viable only with reviewed Git and a disposable writable repository, explicit file/index scope and controls for hooks, signing and configuration. Default Python does not provide the requested Git operation; a draft or stub is not a commit. No live account is inherently necessary for a local commit.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Check type, subject length, imperative phrasing, line limits and privacy. For real creation verify branch, parent, tree contents, object identity and intended file scope using reviewed Git verification. Human review is needed for change coherence and motivation; issue-closing effects require a later appropriate merge.

sources.workflow: Document/type the routed endpoint, align schema with response behavior, migrate all legacy methods on a shared path, optionally change publication metadata, and validate generated artifacts.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The original names Sentry code, drf-spectacular, canonical parameter/response types, ownership and legacy specifications. It explicitly prefers real-token live-endpoint comparisons and lists Make, pnpm, pytest with database reuse, and prek checks. Promotion needs method-specific ownership/publication changes; downstream SDK/connector exposure requires schema regeneration. Linked docs, owning-service source and endpoint tooling are unread.
sources.offline_assessment: A licensed public endpoint repository plus route/response/specification fixtures enables offline schema editing without an account. Authentic generation/tests need reviewed Python and JavaScript dependency closures, project configuration and any isolated test database. Live-token comparison and downstream publication cannot be completed here. Fixture matching is narrower evidence, not live-endpoint verification or published SDK propagation.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Independently compare required/optional/nullable/nested types to authoritative fixtures and sandboxed runtime behavior. Check whole-path migration, references, ownership, generated spec and examples. Endpoint-owner review must approve contract/publication semantics. Only downstream regeneration evidence establishes propagation; live behavior remains unverified.

sources.workflow: Read the complete branch diff and changed files, map input/state boundaries, assess the checklist with context, and report evidence-backed findings without modifying code.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The original calls for a full default-branch-to-head diff using Git and repository metadata, exhaustive changed-file inventory, whole-file reads, surrounding source and existing tests. The service default-branch lookup is its stated acquisition method, not proof hosted access is inherent to analysis. Actual inputs are exact revisions, files, dependency context and review scope.
sources.offline_assessment: An unchanged licensed public repository snapshot and explicit base/head metadata permit offline analysis. Python can read an exported diff; authentic Git diff generation needs reviewed Git expansion. Framework protections and runtime claims need matching dependencies or evidence. No scan, audit or vulnerability finding was performed here; an eventual review cannot promise absence of defects.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Check diff completeness, file/checklist coverage, reachability and whether alleged issues are handled or tested elsewhere. Use narrowly reviewed harmless sandbox reproductions for measurable behavior, never a live target. Severity and relevance remain reviewer judgments; unverified areas must not be marked safe.

sources.workflow: Retrieve unread review-request notifications, retain open unmerged PRs associated with the selected team through requested-reviewer or author membership, and present reasons.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The original explicitly requires authenticated GitHub CLI and uv, a team identifier and organization context, and a bundled fetch script. Its fallback needs notification pages, PR state, requested reviewers and team members. The helper implementation, dependencies and pagination/error semantics are unread; the sample count and records are illustrative.
sources.offline_assessment: The real unread-notification task depends on external account state and service access, both out of scope. An unchanged appropriately licensed public fixture set with notification state, PR status and team relations allows offline Python joins, but unread notifications may be private and unavailable as public input. Do not invent private input or equate fixtures with current requests. Helper dependencies need review before expansion.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Use an independent fixture oracle for unread/reason filtering, open versus merged/closed status, reviewer-team/author-membership joins, multiple teams, empty cases and captured-page completeness. Current account-specific results require authoritative service evidence, not stubs or the fabricated sample output.

sources.workflow: Assess nominated workflows against an external-no-write-access threat model, trace triggering/execution paths, and separate confirmed evidence from unresolved scenarios.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The original needs full workflow definitions, local/composite actions, consumed configuration and surrounding code. It selectively routes to nine unread references. Other-repository workflows and app-installation permissions are noted dependencies outside its scope. Campaign attribution, safe-pattern tables and confidence categories are source-stated empirical claims or policy, not findings verified here.
sources.offline_assessment: A frozen licensed public workflow repository and referenced action/configuration source support offline reading without a hosted account. No workflow execution, scanner, attack construction or audit occurred here. A mechanized model would need reviewed YAML/runtime dependencies, immutable action inputs and strict no-network/no-credential controls; no real runner, token or cloud resource is justified. External action behavior remains a gap until supplied and reviewed.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Check event reachability, attacker capabilities, guards, exact action revisions and claimed paths against captured configuration. Any future measurable reproduction must be harmless and isolated. Confidence/impact require expert judgment; original no-findings wording cannot guarantee security, and the attributed real-world campaign was not independently checked.

sources.workflow: Identify a PR, classify feedback and CI state, fix actionable failures, validate locally, commit/push and monitor until actionable work completes or a human/infrastructure gate is reached.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The original explicitly requires authenticated GitHub CLI, uv, the target repository working directory and scripts for checks, feedback, monitoring and replies. Actual inputs include a PR/branch, logs, threads and check state; local fixes depend on repository-specific tests and linters. Helpers and dependency metadata are unread. Human approval and draft/merge gates are not actionable-CI success conditions.
sources.offline_assessment: State-machine decisions and edits against an immutable public PR/CI transcript can be studied in offline Python. Real monitoring, replies, pushes and fresh feedback need service state and write authorization, forbidden here; stubs cannot complete them. Authentic local fixes require a reviewed repository/dependency closure and scoped commands. Preserve stop conditions rather than simulating a green live PR.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Verify failed/pending/actionable/human-gated classification, feedback priority, no-PR/no-check/draft exits, retry bounds and post-CI feedback. Regression tests can establish a local fix under frozen dependencies. Actual PR success requires authoritative post-push CI and feedback evidence, not local tests or transcript replay.

sources.workflow: Resolve an issue and current/specified PR, extract an optional Linear ticket from a designated linkback comment, preserve the description, and append or replace its issue-reference section.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The original needs an issue identifier/repository, existing PR/body, issue comments with author identity and optionally an explicit PR number. It uses GitHub CLI reads and mutation. Missing Linear linkage permits omission; it does not intrinsically require a Linear account or API. No PR is a stop condition, not permission to create one.
sources.offline_assessment: Python can parse licensed unchanged public issue/comment/body snapshots and produce a deterministic proposed body. Concrete inputs, case handling and section boundaries need review. Authentic PR mutation and confirmation require authorized service access outside scope. An offline replacement body or fake response is not a successful linking operation.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Check idempotence, preservation of unrelated sections, no duplicate issue block, correct repo/issue association, designated author selection and missing-linkback behavior. Validate case sensitivity of ticket extraction against fixtures rather than assume the example command accepts every stated key. Actual mutation needs independent service readback.

sources.workflow: Inspect the full branch change, prepare a reviewer-facing title and cover note, then create a draft PR or refresh an existing one when scope materially changes.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The original explicitly requires authenticated GitHub CLI and branch, working tree, existing PR, base/default branch, commits and full diff inspection. Intended changes should be committed on a feature branch. Verified issue references, existing title/body and rationale are actual input dependencies. Temporary-body-file and create/update examples describe mutations, not only prose generation.
sources.offline_assessment: A complete licensed public branch snapshot/diff and supplied intent permit offline drafting without an account. Python can check formatting, but Git inspection and authentic local commits require reviewed tooling. Even a draft PR is a hosted operation: creation/update remains out of scope. An offline body or mocked response is not a created/updated PR.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Check title conventions, verified references, privacy, compatibility statements and consistency with the entire diff. Human review must judge rationale, risk, organizing principle and usefulness. Publication success needs independently confirmed remote title/body and draft state; drafting success must be labeled separately.

sources.workflow: Build a branded interactive slide application with keyboard navigation and a single-file HTML build, using charts only when supplied content contains real quantitative data.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The original needs topic, slide count, narrative and source data. React/Vite, plugin-react and the single-file plugin are named; Recharts/Charts.jsx are conditional on real chart data. Full design/chart references, exact official logo/glyph SVGs and the Rubik font are unread dependencies. Package examples use ranges, not a frozen closure, and reference remotely served fonts.
sources.offline_assessment: Python-only drafting cannot establish a working native React deck. Reviewed expansion could admit pinned Node/build dependencies, browser tools and licensed unchanged design/font/logo assets, prepositioned with outside access blocked. No hosted account or accelerator is necessary. A self-contained offline artifact must review/resolve remote font references; source or HTML generation alone proves neither native rendering nor faithful branding.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Independently build, inspect single-HTML output and exercise keyboard boundaries, controls, layouts and transitions in a real reviewed browser. Trace every plotted value to supplied data; verify chart files/dependencies are absent for wholly qualitative input. Human visual review is required for branding/readability. Stubs cannot replace native behavior or rendered evidence.

sources.workflow: Define the prompt contract and external context, select a model-family strategy, compare candidate revisions on the same eval slice and select with holdout evidence and an optimization log.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The original needs a prompt/objective, model family/snapshot when known, layer ownership, tools, output schema, constraints and success/failure examples. It routes to unread core patterns, family notes, transformed examples, optimization-loop reference and provenance. Actual empirical optimization needs representative cases, an evaluator and target-model outputs, not just rewritten text.
sources.offline_assessment: Contract extraction, deterministic editing, rubric construction and analysis of existing public eval transcripts can be offline Python work after input/license review. New target-model evaluation is unavailable by default and no model call is authorized. Reviewed local inference would need actual licensed weights, tokenizer, runtime and resource review; a hosted account or accelerator is not automatic. A rewrite alone is not measured optimization.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Independently score baseline/candidates on identical cases with held-out examples, fixed snapshot/settings and explicit cost/latency constraints. Distinguish mechanical format compliance from subjective response quality; use blinded human judgments when needed. Without target-model evidence report candidate drafts and uncertainty, not claimed reliability gains.

sources.workflow: Assess a nominated change for credential-bearing serialized holders and wholesale sinks, tracing existing callers and serialization paths and distinguishing generated conversion from raw attribute access.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The original requires a diff plus full classes, decorators, bases, configuration, constructors, repository-wide sinks and tests. Python/JavaScript references are unread. Its serialization table and severity rules are source guidance, not independently established behavior for every library version. Genuine credentials are unnecessary; harmless sentinel strings suffice for future bounded behavior checks.
sources.offline_assessment: Offline source analysis is feasible on a reviewed licensed public repository without telemetry accounts or services. No serialization review, scan or finding occurred here. Runtime assertions need exact language/library versions and reviewed sandbox commands; standard-library dataclass cases do not establish attrs, Pydantic, JavaScript or SDK semantics. Sinks must remain inert or stubbed with no outside logging.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Use independent sentinel checks against the exact serializer used by a traced path, including repr/str, generated conversion and raw access when relevant. Verify shipped code and diff connection/reachability. Severity and credential semantics require human judgment; field flags, source tables and missing tests alone do not prove safety or a vulnerability.

sources.workflow: Define/review scoped security-model policy using repository evidence, establish exposure and invariants, obtain owner decisions on exclusions/severity, then write and verify only after explicit approval.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The original names a Python resolver normally invoked through uv, repository policies/configuration, deployment/source/test evidence, full docs and any published counterparts. The helper and consuming-policy reference are unread; manual read/search fallback is explicit. Metadata declares Apache-2.0. Owner authority, confirmed target path and approval are governance prerequisites for writing, not facts inferable from a snapshot.
sources.offline_assessment: Python can read a reviewed public snapshot, reconstruct a proposed policy chain and draft unresolved questions. The original forbids repository writing without approval when no approver is available; fixtures cannot invent consent or deployment exposure. Published-doc consistency needs a captured public counterpart before freeze. No hosted account or scanner run is inherent to a bounded draft; no policy was edited or audited here.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Validate scope precedence, explicit parent overrides, stable invariant IDs and named paths/symbols. Code and sandbox tests support particular enforcement claims but cannot prove universal protection. Human owner confirmation must establish exposure, reportability, accepted risks and suppressions. Separate enforcement from monitoring and intended policy from actual security guarantees.

sources.workflow: Assess nominated code/diffs with broader contextual research, account for input provenance and framework mitigations, and distinguish unresolved hypotheses from high-confidence reporting.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The original needs target code, whole-repository context, configuration, upstream validation and framework behavior. Numerous vulnerability/language/infrastructure guides are routed but unread; no scanner executable is mandated. Metadata points to an unread license file and separately attributes reference material to CC BY-SA 4.0, so licensing needs review. Examples/severity tables are guidance, not observed vulnerabilities.
sources.offline_assessment: A concrete immutable licensed public repository permits bounded offline reading/drafting without a cloud account. This research performs no code review, audit, exploit check or scan. Runtime reasoning may require exact framework dependency closures and harmless isolated tests under reviewed controls, never live services. Blanket exceptions and always-flag examples are contextual source claims, not a mechanically valid safety oracle.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Independently establish input control, reachability, validation, framework version and scope before accepting any future finding. Isolated tests can establish specific behavior, not exhaustive absence of vulnerabilities. Expert reviewers must reconcile contextual guidance and thresholds; a no-high-confidence-findings statement is not a security guarantee.

sources.workflow: For eventual adoption assessment, inventory a skill package, combine deterministic scanner leads with contextual reading, and evaluate scope, permissions, scripts and supply-chain claims without confusing threat descriptions with malicious behavior.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The original explicitly requires uv for its bundled scanner, a target skill directory/main document and full package tree. The scanner, PEP 723 dependencies and three reference files are unread. Manual fallback is allowed if the helper fails. Complete assessment needs script contents, links, symlink structure, hooks and package metadata; a lone main document cannot substitute for them.
sources.offline_assessment: No scanner or audit was executed here. Future offline reading is feasible with a concrete unchanged licensed public package, preserved structural metadata and reviewed references. Running the helper needs separate script/dependency review and exact controls before freeze. Inspect symlinks without following them outside fixtures; never execute target hooks, tests or lifecycle scripts. External reputation/provenance needs captured evidence, not live fetching.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Validate deterministic structure/frontmatter against known fixtures and distinguish describing an action from performing it. Intent, necessary permissions and safe-to-install conclusions require human adjudication. Source claims about tool risk, registries, metadata behavior and malicious intent are not guarantees; a clean pattern scan cannot certify adoption safety.

sources.workflow: Choose a minimal creation/revision mode and layout, synthesize source evidence, iterate from examples when needed, author appropriate artifacts, optimize triggers, then register and validate.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The original predominantly routes to unread mode, execution-shape, design, authoring, evaluation and validation references. Actual inputs include operation, repository layout/prior art, source provenance/licenses, contract and positive/negative/holdout examples when iterating. Provider mechanics and official docs are conditional. Workers, hooks and shell preprocessing are optional shapes, not universal requirements or authorization to invoke them.
sources.offline_assessment: Python can draft/edit text and perform simple structural checks on reviewed public input. Full fidelity needs selected reference leaves, specification, registration conventions and validators. Runtime/model trigger evaluation needs a separately reviewed harness and dependency closure; authoring inherently needs no account or accelerator. No skill was edited, registered, executed or evaluated as part of this source-only research.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Check selected-path coverage, direct reference routing, structural schema, registration consistency and should/should-not-trigger fixtures. Establish generated-output/runtime behavior with a reviewed sandbox harness where required; stubbed invocation is not provider execution. Human review must judge source coverage, precision, portability and justified complexity; holdouts are needed for measured improvement claims.

source_reader: Delegated complete-original-body review; exact cohort selection, original hashes, line totals, disjoint IDs and citation bounds independently reconciled by parent.
status_scope: Only original-body prerequisites; linked references, concrete tasks and runtime evidence remain distinct.
